answer: A new identity may join only when two established miners each lock a surety into one shared harbor escrow for four epochs. The newcomer may mine at once, but rewards stay in that harbor until dawn of the fifth epoch, and only if an audit shows its funding, timing, and wording are uncorrelated with both sponsors. A failed audit burns the sureties and escrowed rewards, paying honest auditors. Each sponsor also posts a modest velvet fee, refunded only after a clean audit, and may back at most one newcomer per epoch, so a farm must recruit many independent backers instead of cloning cheap keys.
